newsitem.title: BELARUS: Yeltsin to discuss Belarus with assembly speaker.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to discuss Belarus with assembly speaker.

text.p: Belarussian parliament speaker Semyon Sharetsky said on Wednesday he would speak to Russian President Boris Yeltsin by telephone about the political crisis in Belarus at 11.30 local time (0930 GMT).

He told reporters he planned to travel later on Wednesday to the western Russian city of Smolensk to meet Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and the speakers of both houses of the Russian parliament. But he could not confirm whether Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko would attend.

It was later announced that Yeltsin and Lukashenko had spoken by telephone. The involvement of Yeltsin, still recovering in hospital from heart surgery, followed moves by Russia on Tuesday to defuse the crisis between Lukashenko and his critics.
Tension has been rising in Belarus over Lukashenko's plans to extend his powers in a referendum on November 24. Sharetsky has accused Lukashenko of planning to introduce a dictatorship.
Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday they were alarmed by the worsening confrontation and urged a compromise.
Lukashenko's aides said he had yet to decide whether to attend the Smolensk talks, expected to include Chernomyrdin and the speakers of both houses of the Russian parliament.
